claims.text: The dispute is confined to one line, and identifying it correctly matters. EV-FARE-00710 shows charged_total of SGD 31.00 against quoted_fare_sgd of SGD 25.00, and the four non-ERP lines on that ledger (base 3.80 + distance 14.15 + time 6.25 + platform fee 0.80) sum to exactly 25.00. The entire contested SGD 6.00 is therefore the single ERP pass-through line, and the only questions the tribunal has to decide are the pass-through questions under POL-RD-09 and the POL-RD-11(a) and (b) remedies - not a distance or time question.

The rider does not rest this dispute on a distance or time refund, and the policy closes that route on this record. The governing trace figure on EV-GPS-00710 is trace_distance_km 11.99 against a matched-itinerary optimal of 12.2 km, an excess of -0.21 km that fails both POL-RD-01 establishment tests, and the derived block records the status as 'no deviation'. Because the trip is RYDE_POOL, POL-RD-12 fixes the baseline as the matched-itinerary figure of 12.2 km and not the solo optimal of 8.5 km carried on EV-TRIP-00710, so the 3.7 km pooling difference cannot be claimed as excess either. What survives for the rider on an upfront-quoted trip is the pass-through limb that POL-RD-11(b) expressly preserves.

The rider's account of the booking terms is the only account of them anywhere in the bundle. At 07:28:40, while the trip was still running, the rider sent EV-CHAT-00710 MSG-00710-001 asking why all six dollars were on her booking when the booking said the ERP was shared, and the driver's only answer, MSG-00710-002 at 07:29:05, was 'Pay the full ERP on this booking' - a demand that neither contradicts the sharing term the rider names nor points to any clause or record placing the whole line on this rider. No booking-terms artifact is in the bundle. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion that identifies no artifact and no clause carries no weight, and under POL-RD-11(a) a pass-through line is deductible only to the extent it is properly chargeable.

The gantry match that makes the line chargeable is carried only by the document that bills it. POL-RD-09(4) matches a gantry to the trace by comparing erp_gantry.lat and erp_gantry.lng against the trace, but those coordinates sit on EV-FARE-00710 - the same ledger that charges the SGD 6.00 - and the on_optimal_route flag is carried on that ledger too. The trace proximity reported on EV-GPS-00710 is a nearest fix at 0.0 m distance at the ledger's own charged_at instant of 07:30:40. Nothing independent in the bundle - no gantry registry, no receipt, no advisory - corroborates that this line belongs to this rider's booking.

The trip was a pooled one sharing its route with a second booking, which is exactly the factual setting the rider describes. EV-TRIP-00710 records vehicle_type RYDE_POOL with a matched-itinerary optimal of 12.2 km against a solo optimal of 8.5 km, so 3.7 km of the driven route exists to serve the co-rider that POL-RD-12 contemplates, and the rider said so in the chat at the time. Yet EV-FARE-00710 carries the ERP as one undivided SGD 6.00 line against this rider's booking with no allocation data anywhere in the bundle. On that state of the record the tribunal cannot hold that the whole line has been shown to be properly chargeable to this rider.

If the tribunal regards the allocation as undecidable on this record, the rider's fallback submission is ESCALATE under POL-RD-10 rather than NO_ACTION, because POL-RD-10 is terminal and holds the disputed amount rather than collecting it. That reading is supported by EV-FARE-00710's own note, which states that the POL-RD-09(4) gantry match radius is not a structured field and that 'the ERP figures report amounts and distances and decide no match' - the platform's ledger thus declines to decide the very match on which the charge against this rider survives.

The threshold question under POL-RD-01 is whether any route deviation exists at all, and on this trip's own trace it does not. The governing field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, 11.99 km, measured against the booked optimal of 12.2 km — an excess of -0.21 km (-1.72%). Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute) fail, so no deviation is established and the distance and time lines cannot be disturbed however the rider characterises the trip.

POL-RD-08 puts the initial burden on the rider to show both that the artifacts describe the same trip and that the excess meets the POL-RD-01 threshold. The identifiers match, but the second limb fails on a trace that is admitted at weight 1.0, 100% coverage, no gaps and no sampling failures. The burden therefore never shifts to the driver, and the rider's claim is not sustained on the record.

This is a RYDE_POOL trip, so the POL-RD-01 baseline is the matched-itinerary optimal of 12.2 km recorded at match time, not the 8.5 km solo-rider optimal carried for reference only. Distance attributable to collecting or setting down the co-rider the claim refers to is expressly excluded from excess. Measured against the correct pool baseline the trace runs 0.21 km SHORT of optimal — the rider cannot turn the very pooling he booked into a deviation.

The contested SGD 6 is a metered pass-through for a single gantry, 'Matched itinerary gantry', which lies on the optimal route and which the trace actually crossed: the nearest driver fix is 0.0 m from the gantry coordinates at 07:30:40, far inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 uses. A crossed, on-optimal-route gantry line is properly chargeable under POL-RD-09 and there is no billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4), because the trace does pass the line.

This trip is UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 25.00 and total_charged 31.00, so under POL-RD-11 POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large any excess might be. The only head of refund is the amount by which the charge exceeds the quote after properly chargeable pass-through lines: 31.00 - 25.00 - 6.00 of crossed on-route ERP = 0.00. The whole quote-to-charge difference is the ERP line itself, and that line is properly chargeable under POL-RD-09.

The relief the rider actually seeks is a pro-rata split of the gantry charge between two passengers. The loaded policy provides no such remedy: POL-RD-09 settles ERP gantry-by-gantry as a metered third-party pass-through, and POL-RD-12's pooled-trip provision adjusts only the distance baseline. Neither clause licenses an allocation of an ERP line between co-riders, so the claim asks for a remedy the policy does not provide and must fail on that ground alone.

The chat log does not help the rider. Its only two messages are the rider's question at 07:28:40 and the driver's answer at 07:29:05; neither records any rider instruction to avoid the gantry or take another road, so POL-RD-04 (rider-requested detour) is engaged on neither side and no waypoint is in play. The driver's statement that the gantry was crossed on the matched itinerary is in fact corroborated by the trace.

EV-ADVIS-00710-01 is MISSING — no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window — and it carries weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so its absence is citable but can carry no fact. The driver asserts no external traffic cause and relies on no advisory; the absence is therefore neutral and leaves the trace-based analysis above untouched.

No repeat-deviation pattern is available against this driver even if the profile check were reached: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250. POL-RD-06 is consulted only on a MATERIAL deviation, and none exists here, so no POL-RD-06(a) balance-shift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises. No other profile field is relied on, and none may ground a finding under POL-GEN-01.

The ruling value that follows is NO_ACTION. On this rider-filed dispute the present state is fare_breakdown.payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00; under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION leaves that state exactly as it stands and never creates or restores a refund. The disputed SGD 6 accordingly stands charged.

ruling.explanation: To the rider: I have considered your point that the pool booking said the ERP was shared and that another rider was aboard. The contested SGD 6.00 is the only ERP line on the bill. Your trip was an upfront quote of SGD 25.00 (base SGD 3.80 + distance SGD 14.15 + time SGD 6.25 + platform fee SGD 0.80 = SGD 25.00 exactly), and the charged total was SGD 31.00, the extra being the SGD 6.00 ERP pass-through. Under POL-RD-11 an upfront-quoted, quoted_fare 25.00 trip gives no distance-or-time refund, so the only question is whether the SGD 6.00 ERP line is properly chargeable. It is. The single gantry ('Matched itinerary gantry') lies on the matched-itinerary optimal route, and the GPS trace passes it: the nearest fix is 0.0 m from the gantry coordinates at 07:30:40, inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09(4) applies. That makes it a crossed, on-route gantry, not a phantom line, so no billing-integrity refund arises and the POL-RD-11(a) arithmetic is charged_total 31.00 - quoted_fare 25.00 - properly chargeable ERP 6.00 = 0.00. Your argument that the gantry coordinates sit only on the ledger that bills them does not change this: POL-RD-09(4) prescribes exactly that comparison, and the trace independently places a fix at the gantry at the charged instant. Your request for a pro-rata share fails for a separate reason - the policy contains no mechanism to split a metered ERP pass-through between co-riders. POL-RD-12 (pooled trips) adjusts only the distance baseline and does not touch ERP, and no booking-terms artifact showing a shared-ERP term exists in the bundle; the only source for that term is your own message. I also cannot find a distance deviation: the governing trace figure is 11.99 km against the matched-itinerary optimal of 12.2 km, an excess of -0.21 km (-1.72%), which fails both POL-RD-01 tests, and the 8.5 km solo optimal is not the baseline for a RYDE_POOL trip. Your fallback request for ESCALATE is declined: no POL-RD-10 trigger fires (see below). To the driver: the ERP line stands as charged, and your statement that the gantry was crossed on the matched itinerary is corroborated by the trace. Your chat message 'Pay the full ERP on this booking' does not affect the outcome - the line is chargeable because the trace crossed an on-route gantry, not because you demanded payment. No POL-RD-04 rider-requested detour is in play (the chat contains no instruction, and no waypoint), and no POL-RD-06 conduct referral arises: there is no material deviation and no repeat pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0 over completed_trips_90d 250). On escalation, POL-RD-10 is not engaged: the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) (100% coverage, no gaps, 10 s sampling), the trip identifiers and timestamps agree across the trip record, trace and ledger, no refund computation exceeds any ceiling, and the ERP line has its counterpart in the trace. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00710-01, weight 0.0) is neutral, since neither party asserted an external traffic cause; and the ledger's note that the gantry match radius is not a structured field is a data-modelling note, not a finding that the match is undecidable - POL-RD-09(4) supplies the test and the record satisfies it. Result: the charge stands. payment_status remains CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd remains 0.00. Confidence 0.90, capped by the weight-1.0 artifacts that carry the deciding fact (the GPS trace and the fare breakdown).

To both parties: the disputed SGD 6.00 ERP line stands and no refund is due. The figures I used are all from EV-FARE-00710 — quoted fare SGD 25.00, charged total SGD 31.00, one ERP line of SGD 6.00. The four non-ERP lines (base 3.80 + distance 14.15 + time 6.25 + platform fee 0.80) sum exactly to the SGD 25.00 quote, so the SGD 6.00 ERP line is the whole of the difference and the whole of the dispute. That much of the rider's case is accepted.

Route: this is a RYDE_POOL trip, so under POL-RD-12 the POL-RD-01 baseline is the matched-itinerary optimal of 12.2 km on EV-TRIP-00710, not the solo optimal of 8.5 km, which is carried for reference only. The governing trace figure on EV-GPS-00710 (trace_distance_km 11.99) runs 0.21 km short of that baseline, -1.72%, so both POL-RD-01 establishment tests fail and no deviation exists. POL-RD-06 was not reached, so no conduct referral arises, and the rider was right not to press a distance or time refund.

Fare model: this is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip, so POL-RD-11 governs and POL-RD-02 does not run — the distance and time lines were fixed at booking and no distance-or-time refund is available however the trip is characterised. The rider's only heads of recovery are POL-RD-11(a) and a POL-RD-09 pass-through correction. The POL-RD-11(a) arithmetic is 31.00 (charged_total) less 25.00 (quoted_fare) less 6.00 (properly chargeable ERP) = 0.00. The single 'Matched itinerary gantry' line is on the optimal route and the trace passes within 0.0 m of the gantry at 07:30:40, so it is properly chargeable under POL-RD-09 and there is no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity defect. The rider's point that the gantry coordinates and the on-optimal flag live on the billing ledger is answered: the crossing is established by the trace's own fix at the gantry location (EV-GPS-00710, nearest fix 0.0 m at the charged instant), which is independent of the ledger, and the fare breakdown's note that the 250 m match radius is not a structured field does not make the match undecidable.

The rider's claim that the booking said the ERP was shared, and the pro-rata split that would follow, is not supported. There is no booking-terms artifact anywhere in the bundle, and an assertion that cites no artifact carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The driver's chat reply at 07:29:05 ('Pay the full ERP on this booking') is a demand, not an admission, and the counterparty statement merely confirms the gantry crossing the ledger already records. Nor does the loaded policy provide the remedy sought: POL-RD-09 settles ERP gantry-by-gantry as a metered third-party pass-through, and POL-RD-12 adjusts only the distance baseline and excludes co-rider collection distance from excess — neither clause allocates an ERP line between co-riders. The driver's submissions on the trace, the pooled baseline, the POL-RD-11 arithmetic and the absence of any pro-rata ERP remedy are accepted.

The rider's fallback of ESCALATE under POL-RD-10 is refused because no trigger fires: the trip identifiers match across EV-TRIP-00710, EV-GPS-00710 and EV-FARE-00710; the trace is not impaired (100% coverage, no gaps, 10-second sampling); no timestamps conflict; no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact; the refund does not approach the POL-RD-10(6) ceiling; and the ERP line has a counterpart in the trace, so POL-RD-10(8) does not apply.

On admissibility, no artifact below weight 1.0 carries a deciding fact; the cap is therefore 1.0. EV-ADVIS-00710-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT): it carries no fact, is not relied on, and since no external traffic cause was asserted, POL-RD-13 leaves the trace-based analysis untouched. Outcome: the present state stands — payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00 is left exactly as it is.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: the dispute is the SGD 6.00 ERP gantry charge on trip TRP-00710 (a RYDE_POOL, upfront-quoted booking). I find the charge stands and no part of it is refundable.

Distance and time. The trip was UPFRONT_QUOTE, so under POL-RD-11 the distance and time lines were fixed at booking (charged_total SGD 31.00 against quoted_fare_sgd SGD 25.00, EV-FARE-00710) and no distance-or-time refund exists however the route ran. In any event there was no deviation: the governing trace figure on EV-GPS-00710 is trace_distance_km 11.99 against the booked optimal of 12.2 km on EV-TRIP-00710, an excess of -0.21 km (-1.72%). Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests fail (neither greater than 20% nor greater than 0.8 km), so no deviation is established. Because the trip is pooled, POL-RD-12 fixes the baseline as the matched-itinerary optimal of 12.2 km and not the solo-rider optimal of 8.5 km carried for reference; the 3.7 km pooling difference is expressly excluded from excess.

The ERP line. The contested SGD 6.00 is a single line, 'Matched itinerary gantry', on EV-FARE-00710. That gantry lies on the optimal route and the driver's trace passed within 0.0 m of it at 07:30:40 (EV-GPS-00710), far inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 prescribes. It is therefore a properly chargeable pass-through. Under POL-RD-11(a) the only head of refund is charged_total (31.00) less quoted_fare (25.00) less properly chargeable pass-throughs (6.00) = 0.00, which is what the ledger itself computes.

The rider's central point. The rider says the pool booking described the ERP as shared, so only a share should fall on her. The loaded policy gives no such remedy: POL-RD-09 settles ERP gantry-by-gantry as a metered third-party pass-through, and POL-RD-12 adjusts only the pooled distance baseline, not the allocation of an ERP line between co-riders. There is also no booking-terms artifact in the bundle recording the term; the only account of it is the rider's own chat message (MSG-00710-001), and the driver's reply 'Pay the full ERP on this booking' (MSG-00710-002) neither establishes nor concedes it. Even taking the rider's account as true, no clause would convert it into a refund, so the claim is not supported on this record.

The rider's two further arguments are answered together. First, that the gantry match is carried only by the ledger that bills it: POL-RD-09(4) prescribes exactly that comparison (erp_gantry coordinates against the trace, 250 m), the gantry carries coordinates, and the trace crosses it, so the clause's own test runs and finds the line matched. Second, the fallback submission that the allocation is undecidable and the case should ESCALATE under POL-RD-10: none of POL-RD-10's triggers fires. The trip identifiers all match TRP-00710, the trace is unimpaired (100% coverage, no gaps, 0.0 s maximum gap, 145 fixes), timestamps are consistent, the ledger's own note about an unstructured match radius does not make the match undecidable where the coordinates and the trace crossing are both on record, and no charge line is unmatched. The escalation route is closed.

Billing integrity and conduct. There is no POL-RD-09(4) defect: the trace does pass the gantry, so the line is not phantom. There is no repeat-deviation pattern (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d 0 over completed_trips_90d 250), no MATERIAL deviation, and therefore no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00710-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; neither party asserts an external traffic cause or relies on it, so its absence carries no fact and does not affect the outcome. No artifact below weight 1.0 carries any deciding fact here, so no discount applies to the finding.

Decision. The rider's claim is not supported by the evidence and the present state stands: NO_ACTION. Payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 are left exactly as they are; the SGD 6.00 gantry line stands charged. The figures used are charged_total 31.00, quoted_fare_sgd 25.00, the ERP line 6.00, trace_distance_km 11.99, matched-itinerary optimal 12.2 km and solo optimal 8.5 km.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties, here is the decision on this rider-filed dispute.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DISPUTED. The contested item is the single SGD 6.00 ERP line on EV-FARE-00710, inside a total charge of SGD 31.00 against a quoted fare of SGD 25.00. The other four lines — base SGD 3.80 + distance SGD 14.15 + time SGD 6.25 + platform fee SGD 0.80 — sum to exactly SGD 25.00, so the rider has correctly identified the one line in issue. Whether it is properly chargeable is the whole case.

NO ROUTE DEVIATION. This was a RYDE_POOL booking on an upfront quote (EV-TRIP-00710; EV-FARE-00710 fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 25.00). Under POL-RD-12 the baseline for a pooled trip is the matched-itinerary optimal of 12.2 km on EV-TRIP-00710, not the solo optimal of 8.5 km carried for reference only. Measured against that baseline, the governing trace figure (POL-RD-01: gps_trace.trace_distance_km) is 11.99 km on EV-GPS-00710 — 0.21 km short of optimal, and the derived status is 'no deviation'. No deviation exists, so no distance or time line can be disturbed.

THE ERP LINE IS PROPERLY CHARGEABLE. On an upfront quote POL-RD-11 governs and POL-RD-02 does not run. POL-RD-11(a) refunds only the amount by which charged_total exceeds the quote plus the pass-through lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. Here 31.00 − 25.00 = 6.00, and the only pass-through line is the ERP crossing itself. The gantry 'Matched itinerary gantry' lies on the optimal route (EV-FARE-00710, on_optimal_route true), and the trace passes it: the nearest driver fix on EV-GPS-00710 is 0.0 m from the gantry coordinates at 07:30:40, the charged instant, far inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 uses. The line is therefore properly chargeable, the 6.00 difference is absorbed by it, and the POL-RD-11(a) figure is 31.00 − 25.00 − 6.00 = 0.00, matching the ledger's own pol_rd_11_remedy of 0.00. There is no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity defect, because the trace does pass the gantry.

THE RIDER'S SHARING POINT. The rider's central claim — that the pool booking said the ERP was shared with the co-rider, so only part of the SGD 6.00 should fall on her — is not supported by any artifact and finds no remedy in the policy. The only record of the term is her own chat message of 07:28:40 (EV-CHAT-00710, MSG-00710-001), and the driver's reply of 07:29:05 does not contradict it; but neither message evidences the booking terms, and no booking-terms artifact is in the bundle. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion that identifies no supporting artifact carries no weight. In any event the policy gives no pro-rata allocation of an ERP line between co-riders: POL-RD-09 settles ERP gantry-by-gantry as a metered third-party pass-through, and POL-RD-12 adjusts only the distance baseline. The claim asks for a remedy the policy does not provide. The rider's related submission that the gantry match is carried only by the billing document is rejected: the match is made against the trace, and EV-GPS-00710 places the vehicle on the gantry at the charged instant.

NO ESCALATION. The rider's fallback request for ESCALATE under POL-RD-10 is refused; no trigger fires. The artifacts all carry trip identifier TRP-00710; the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c) (100% coverage, no gaps, 10 s sampling, no jumps); timestamps agree; no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing or fieldless artifact; the POL-RD-11(a) figure does not exceed the charge; and every charge line has a counterpart in the trace and trip record. The ledger's note that the gantry match radius is not a structured field means only that the ledger publishes amounts and distances and does not itself decide the match — under POL-RD-09 the match is made against the trace, and the trace decides it. The missing advisory EV-ADVIS-00710-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) is neutral: no party asserts an external traffic cause, so it neither exonerates the driver nor escalates the matter.

PROFILES. The driver's profile shows deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 250, so no POL-RD-06 pattern arises and no conduct referral is made; no other profile field grounds any finding (POL-GEN-01).

RULING. NO_ACTION. On this rider-filed dispute the fare_breakdown state (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) stands exactly as it is, and the SGD 6.00 ERP line remains charged. No refund issues and no driver compensation is payable. Confidence 0.90, resting on the weight-1.0 artifacts EV-FARE-00710, EV-GPS-00710 and EV-TRIP-00710 that carry the deciding facts; the 0.70 escalation floor is not approached.

ledger.claim: The dispute is confined to one line, and identifying it correctly matters. EV-FARE-00710 shows charged_total of SGD 31.00 against quoted_fare_sgd of SGD 25.00, and the four non-ERP lines on that ledger (base 3.80 + distance 14.15 + time 6.25 + platform fee 0.80) sum to exactly 25.00. The entire contested SGD 6.00 is therefore the single ERP pass-through line, and the only questions the tribunal has to decide are the pass-through questions under POL-RD-09 and the POL-RD-11(a) and (b) remedies - not a distance or time question.

The rider does not rest this dispute on a distance or time refund, and the policy closes that route on this record. The governing trace figure on EV-GPS-00710 is trace_distance_km 11.99 against a matched-itinerary optimal of 12.2 km, an excess of -0.21 km that fails both POL-RD-01 establishment tests, and the derived block records the status as 'no deviation'. Because the trip is RYDE_POOL, POL-RD-12 fixes the baseline as the matched-itinerary figure of 12.2 km and not the solo optimal of 8.5 km carried on EV-TRIP-00710, so the 3.7 km pooling difference cannot be claimed as excess either. What survives for the rider on an upfront-quoted trip is the pass-through limb that POL-RD-11(b) expressly preserves.

The rider's account of the booking terms is the only account of them anywhere in the bundle. At 07:28:40, while the trip was still running, the rider sent EV-CHAT-00710 MSG-00710-001 asking why all six dollars were on her booking when the booking said the ERP was shared, and the driver's only answer, MSG-00710-002 at 07:29:05, was 'Pay the full ERP on this booking' - a demand that neither contradicts the sharing term the rider names nor points to any clause or record placing the whole line on this rider. No booking-terms artifact is in the bundle. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion that identifies no artifact and no clause carries no weight, and under POL-RD-11(a) a pass-through line is deductible only to the extent it is properly chargeable.

The gantry match that makes the line chargeable is carried only by the document that bills it. POL-RD-09(4) matches a gantry to the trace by comparing erp_gantry.lat and erp_gantry.lng against the trace, but those coordinates sit on EV-FARE-00710 - the same ledger that charges the SGD 6.00 - and the on_optimal_route flag is carried on that ledger too. The trace proximity reported on EV-GPS-00710 is a nearest fix at 0.0 m distance at the ledger's own charged_at instant of 07:30:40. Nothing independent in the bundle - no gantry registry, no receipt, no advisory - corroborates that this line belongs to this rider's booking.

The trip was a pooled one sharing its route with a second booking, which is exactly the factual setting the rider describes. EV-TRIP-00710 records vehicle_type RYDE_POOL with a matched-itinerary optimal of 12.2 km against a solo optimal of 8.5 km, so 3.7 km of the driven route exists to serve the co-rider that POL-RD-12 contemplates, and the rider said so in the chat at the time. Yet EV-FARE-00710 carries the ERP as one undivided SGD 6.00 line against this rider's booking with no allocation data anywhere in the bundle. On that state of the record the tribunal cannot hold that the whole line has been shown to be properly chargeable to this rider.

If the tribunal regards the allocation as undecidable on this record, the rider's fallback submission is ESCALATE under POL-RD-10 rather than NO_ACTION, because POL-RD-10 is terminal and holds the disputed amount rather than collecting it. That reading is supported by EV-FARE-00710's own note, which states that the POL-RD-09(4) gantry match radius is not a structured field and that 'the ERP figures report amounts and distances and decide no match' - the platform's ledger thus declines to decide the very match on which the charge against this rider survives.

The threshold question under POL-RD-01 is whether any route deviation exists at all, and on this trip's own trace it does not. The governing field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, 11.99 km, measured against the booked optimal of 12.2 km — an excess of -0.21 km (-1.72%). Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute) fail, so no deviation is established and the distance and time lines cannot be disturbed however the rider characterises the trip.

POL-RD-08 puts the initial burden on the rider to show both that the artifacts describe the same trip and that the excess meets the POL-RD-01 threshold. The identifiers match, but the second limb fails on a trace that is admitted at weight 1.0, 100% coverage, no gaps and no sampling failures. The burden therefore never shifts to the driver, and the rider's claim is not sustained on the record.

This is a RYDE_POOL trip, so the POL-RD-01 baseline is the matched-itinerary optimal of 12.2 km recorded at match time, not the 8.5 km solo-rider optimal carried for reference only. Distance attributable to collecting or setting down the co-rider the claim refers to is expressly excluded from excess. Measured against the correct pool baseline the trace runs 0.21 km SHORT of optimal — the rider cannot turn the very pooling he booked into a deviation.

The contested SGD 6 is a metered pass-through for a single gantry, 'Matched itinerary gantry', which lies on the optimal route and which the trace actually crossed: the nearest driver fix is 0.0 m from the gantry coordinates at 07:30:40, far inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 uses. A crossed, on-optimal-route gantry line is properly chargeable under POL-RD-09 and there is no billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4), because the trace does pass the line.

This trip is UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 25.00 and total_charged 31.00, so under POL-RD-11 POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large any excess might be. The only head of refund is the amount by which the charge exceeds the quote after properly chargeable pass-through lines: 31.00 - 25.00 - 6.00 of crossed on-route ERP = 0.00. The whole quote-to-charge difference is the ERP line itself, and that line is properly chargeable under POL-RD-09.

The relief the rider actually seeks is a pro-rata split of the gantry charge between two passengers. The loaded policy provides no such remedy: POL-RD-09 settles ERP gantry-by-gantry as a metered third-party pass-through, and POL-RD-12's pooled-trip provision adjusts only the distance baseline. Neither clause licenses an allocation of an ERP line between co-riders, so the claim asks for a remedy the policy does not provide and must fail on that ground alone.

The chat log does not help the rider. Its only two messages are the rider's question at 07:28:40 and the driver's answer at 07:29:05; neither records any rider instruction to avoid the gantry or take another road, so POL-RD-04 (rider-requested detour) is engaged on neither side and no waypoint is in play. The driver's statement that the gantry was crossed on the matched itinerary is in fact corroborated by the trace.

EV-ADVIS-00710-01 is MISSING — no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window — and it carries weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so its absence is citable but can carry no fact. The driver asserts no external traffic cause and relies on no advisory; the absence is therefore neutral and leaves the trace-based analysis above untouched.

No repeat-deviation pattern is available against this driver even if the profile check were reached: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250. POL-RD-06 is consulted only on a MATERIAL deviation, and none exists here, so no POL-RD-06(a) balance-shift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises. No other profile field is relied on, and none may ground a finding under POL-GEN-01.

The ruling value that follows is NO_ACTION. On this rider-filed dispute the present state is fare_breakdown.payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00; under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION leaves that state exactly as it stands and never creates or restores a refund. The disputed SGD 6 accordingly stands charged.
